paper_metadata.title: Ta-alloying for the construction of fully eutectic structure to enhance the broad-temperature tribological performance of CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy: A systematic study on compositional and structural evolutions

evidence.quote: The CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloys (HEAs) often suffer from significant wear at high temperatures due to their low strength and thermal softening behavior.
Two types of HEA ingots were synthesized, namely CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeNiTa0.4 (in atomic ratio), which are designated as Ta0 and Ta0.4, respectively, based on the content of Ta atoms.

Eutectic HEAs typically consist of alternating soft and hard dual-phase structures. Generally, the soft phase is a solid solution composed of multiple elements, while the hard phase is an intermetallic compound that lies between ceramics and metals

Within a certain range, according to Archard’s law, the wear resistance of a material is positively correlated with the surface hardness of the alloy.
